references.text: The commandment to observe a feast as an eternal ordinance throughout all generations, using language similar to 'בְּרִית עוֹלָם' (everlasting covenant).
The context of the Sabbath commandment as a sign between God and the children of Israel throughout all generations.
The continuation of the Sabbath covenant as an eternal sign between the Lord and the children of Israel.
The Sabbath is referred to as an everlasting covenant; the same expression 'בְּרִית עוֹלָם' is used.
The repetition of the Sabbath commandment in Deuteronomy with a command to keep the Sabbath day holy.
A prophetic promise to those who keep the Sabbath and hold fast to God's covenant.
Blessings associated with honoring the Sabbath and calling it a delight.
The Sabbath given as a sign between God and Israel, parallel to the Exodus text.
Reiteration of the Sabbath as a sign so that they may know that the Lord is their God.
Nehemiah reminds the people that God made His holy Sabbath known to them.
The New Testament fulfillment of the Sabbath rest that awaits for God's people.
Both establish God's ordinances as 'everlasting' for the children of Israel throughout all generations.
A strong linguistic and theological parallel: holy means/times that apply 'throughout all generations'.
Extends the concept of the Sabbath from a human covenant to the rest of the land (Jubilee year), both for the Lord's sake.
